walkthroughs.body_html:
Time & the Calendar — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Time & the Calendar brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Time & the Calendar.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many planets are in the Solar System (IAU 2006)?
Who proposed the heliocentric model in 1543?
options: Galileo
Copernicus
Kepler
Ptolemy
A literal horizon you can walk to.
How long a star lives.
A unit of DISTANCE - the distance light travels in one year.
A unit of time.

mcqs.q: What does cosmological redshift tell us?
options: Light gets tired and loses energy.
A literal horizon you can walk to.
Galaxies are turning red as they age.
Galaxies are receding from us due to the expansion of space.

mcqs.q: What is a black hole's event horizon?
options: The visible 'edge' of the black hole.
Light gets tired and loses energy.
A literal horizon you can walk to.
The boundary beyond which not even light can escape.
